newsitem.title: CANADA: British Columbia lumber negotiators split on wages.
newsitem.headline: British Columbia lumber negotiators split on wages.

text.p: Contract negotiators for British Columbia's coastal forestry companies and the lumber workers union remain far apart on the issue of wages, but will keep pressing for a deal, sources said on Thursday.
Forest Industrial Relations, which bargains on behalf of 65 forestry companies, said it sweetened its wage offer in talks today.
It is proposing no wage increase in the first year, a 1.5 percent raise in the second and two percent in the third. It previously offered only 1.5 percent in the third year.
"Certainly one of the main issues is the wage spread between us...(but) we're going to continue to pursue an agreement," said Keith Bennett, chief negotiator for Forest Industrial Relations.
He said two or three other issues were also obstacles in the talks but declined to name them.
The IWA-Canada union which represents 29,000 lumber workers has proposed wage increases of 2.0, 2.5 and 3.0 percent a year. It opposes the companies' effort to have no increase in the first year.
But the union has not moved to call a strike vote and the two sides have been meeting on an almost daily basis. Both sides said they thought a deal was unlikely before next week at the earliest.
